correctness.rationale: The unrestricted published four-state direction-determinate shortest-accepted-word maximum is binomial(4,2)-1=5. Direct independent simulation of the specified binary witness verifies its first accepted word is abba, length four; the ternary witness first accepts abbac, length five. For the binary upper bound, independently coded exhaustive C++ enumeration treats each of the four direction splits, all 625^2 two-letter transition-map pairs, all independently chosen left/right endmarker return maps (superset of actual machines), and both symmetry-inequivalent singleton accepting states when available; 101,562,500 configurations yielded exact split maxima 0,3,4,3. Singleton final state reduction is safe because any accepted shortest word remains accepted while no new shorter word appears. Initial state normalization and end-marker independent returns only enlarge the checked class. Hence no binary four-state machine reaches five. The published unrestricted upper bound and ternary construction finish the exact minimum alphabet proof.
